scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, indicating no tariff/rate change is logged.

F-03.statement: Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 had read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 had read_type ACTUAL, per billing-db.disputed_bills_by_read_type.

F-04.statement: ACTUAL-read bills form the majority (~59%) of disputed bills, exceeding ESTIMATED-read disputed bills.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute_response_times for 2440 tickets shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-07.statement: Service contract §4.2 provides that the utility may request route priority changes, executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager.

F-08.statement: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle returned 320 account records (account_id, route only) spanning 40 distinct routes; no read_type, tariff, or import-status fields were present.

F-09.statement: route-log.lagging_routes returned 14 route records (fields completion, route), each with a distinct completion value; sample record is route R-00 at completion 0.70.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-AI-AUTO-ANSWER-FIX.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response capacity problem, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets (and auto-fixes bills) is the appropriate solution.

H-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is causing reads to be rejected or misclassified, producing incorrect bills and driving disputes.

H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: The MDMS/AMI nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) started failing or delivering invalid reads, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-COMPLETION-DROP.statement: Manual meter-read route completion by the contracted field service dropped since August, increasing estimate substitutions and billing errors.

H-BILLS-CORRECT-EXTERNAL-DRIVE.statement: Bills issued since August are substantively correct, and the ticket surge is driven by a non-pipeline factor (e.g., a tariff/rate or billing-cycle change) rather than any read/validation defect.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: Disputed bills are predominantly tied to ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads (1785 of 3025), so the root cause likely lies in how actual reads are processed/billed (e.g., import validation misclassification or rate application) rather than in estimate substitution.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-completion log (E-01) shows manual-read completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts for Aug-Sep 2026, indicating a real shortfall in field read coverage that could drive estimate substitutions and incorrect bills.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff or rate change was logged in that system; this is evidence against the tariff-change explanation that H-BILLS-CORRECT-EXTERNAL-DRIVE offered as a non-pipeline cause of the dispute surge, though a billing-cycle change (the other example in that hypothesis) remains untested.

Billing-db shows 3025 disputed bills split by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED and 1785 ACTUAL, so a majority (≈59%) of disputed bills carried an ACTUAL (non-estimated) read rather than an estimate substitution. This caps how much of the dispute surge estimate-substitution causes (field read drop, AMI delivery failure) can explain, since those mechanisms only produce ESTIMATED-type bills.

CRM data (E-04) shows median dispute-ticket response time of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets. This indicates response handling is currently meeting its SLA, not an overloaded/slow process, which undercuts the premise that the surge stems from slow ticket response needing an auto-answer agent.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly (E-05) shows disputes went from 610 (Jun) and 590 (Jul) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026, confirming the magnitude of the dispute surge referenced in the initial request. This authoritative tool record substantiates that a real, large volume increase occurred coincident with August but reveals nothing about which causal mechanism produced it.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's unverified claim that no tariff change occurred this year aligns directionally with the authoritative tool finding (E-02: zero tariff_change_log records), but as a non-authoritative stakeholder statement it adds no independent evidentiary weight and does not address the untested billing-cycle-change alternative also named in H-BILLS-CORRECT-EXTERNAL-DRIVE.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (interview, E-07) attributes late routes and resulting estimated bills to a staffing shortfall of three readers since July. This is an unverified stakeholder claim, not a tool record, and it comes from a stakeholder with a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the existing governance arrangement already encoded in constraint K-DISPATCH: the utility may request field route priority changes but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD). This document is about authorization/process control for push_route_update, not about any mechanism driving the billing dispute surge.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-09 shows billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query returned 320 accounts (all with ESTIMATED-type bills last cycle) spread across 40 routes, but the record only carries account_id and route fields — no read_type, tariff, or import-status fields. This means the query run for W-WI-1 (intended to diagnose the ACTUAL-read billing-processing defect) instead surfaced ESTIMATED-cycle account/route data, which is more relevant to the field-route/estimate-substitution path than to the ACTUAL-read majority (1785/3025, E-03) the root problem centers on.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) returns 14 routes each with a distinct completion value below full completion, e.g. route R-00 at 0.70, giving route-level granularity under the 0.88-vs-0.95 aggregate shortfall (E-01); the record exposes which/how many routes lag but says nothing about why (staffing vs other) or how much they contribute to ESTIMATED-type disputed bills.

U-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE-TIMIN.question: Did billing import validation rules change around August in a way that caused ACTUAL-read misclassification or rate misapplication (H-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE is untested)?
U-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE-TIMIN.decision_impact: Determines whether the fix targets import validation logic or rate-application logic; without it the specific processing defect cannot be identified or corrected.
U-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE-TIMIN.resolution_path: Query billing-config validation rule change log for changes coincident with Aug 2026 and cross-reference against the ACTUAL-read disputed bills in E-03.
U-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE-TIMIN.safe_placeholder: Treat H-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE as a candidate mechanism only; restrict scope to read-only diagnosis until the specific defect is confirmed.

U-FIELD-ROUTE-DROP-CAUSE.question: Is the field route completion drop (0.88 vs 0.95) actually caused by the staffing shortage SH-FIELD claims, and how much does it contribute to ESTIMATED-type disputes?
U-FIELD-ROUTE-DROP-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether any remediation for ESTIMATED-type disputes should target field staffing/scheduling versus another cause.
U-FIELD-ROUTE-DROP-CAUSE.resolution_path: Cross-check route-log schedule/staffing records against SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-07, unverified) and route-level timing data.
U-FIELD-ROUTE-DROP-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the field-route contribution to disputes as partial and unconfirmed, limited to the ESTIMATED-type share only.

U-AMI-DELIVERY-STATUS.question: Are AMI/MDMS read delivery failures contributing to incorrect reads (H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE)?
U-AMI-DELIVERY-STATUS.decision_impact: Determines whether AMI/vendor-side delivery issues should be included in the root-cause diagnosis once data access is available.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-STATUS.resolution_path: Once vendor provisions mdms-export access (currently DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING with no fallback), compare MDMS read-event timestamps to billing import records.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-STATUS.safe_placeholder: Exclude AMI-sourced causal claims from root-cause conclusions until vendor access is granted and verified (KNOWN_LIMITATION).

U-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY.question: Is dispute-ticket-volume reduction a valid proxy for restored billing accuracy, or could volume fall for unrelated reasons (e.g., customer behavior)?
U-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether dispute-volume recovery alone can be used to confirm the fix worked, or whether the ACTUAL-read dispute share must also be tracked.
U-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Track the ACTUAL-read dispute share (M-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-SHARE) alongside monthly volume after any fix to confirm the mechanism, not just the symptom, improved.
U-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Do not treat volume decline alone as proof of root-cause resolution; require the ACTUAL-read dispute share to also normalize.

U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-FIELD-BILL handoff (daily manual-read upload) delivering semantically valid, complete data to billing, given its delivery_status and semantic_validity are UNKNOWN?
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff is degraded, the route-completion figures (E-01) and resulting billing diagnosis for manual-read accounts could be understated or misattributed.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Verify H-FIELD-BILL delivery_status/semantic_validity by cross-checking route-log completion records against billing-db import timestamps for Aug-Sep.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat E-01 route-completion figures as provisional pending handoff validity confirmation; do not finalize field-route conclusions on them alone.

U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-MDMS-BILL handoff (nightly AMI export) delivering semantically valid data to billing, given its delivery_status and semantic_validity are UNKNOWN?
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff is degraded it could itself be a source of ACTUAL-read billing errors distinct from import validation rule changes.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Validate H-MDMS-BILL delivery_status/semantic_validity once vendor access is granted via mdms-export, comparing export timestamps to billing import records.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Do not attribute ACTUAL-read billing errors to AMI handoff failure until this is validated; keep as an open candidate (KNOWN_LIMITATION).
